results.title: Nkrumah Launches Positive Action Campaign and General Strike
results.note: Campaign launched 8 Jan 1950; general strike confirmed; Nkrumah arrested and imprisoned.

results.title: CPP Sweeps Gold Coast Election — Nkrumah Released from Prison
results.note: CPP won 34 of 38 contested seats; Nkrumah released 12 Feb 1951 and appointed Leader of Government Business. Event says 34 seats — correct.

results.title: Nkrumah Formally Appointed Prime Minister of the Gold Coast
results.note: Constitutional amendment 10 Mar 1952; Nkrumah elected PM by Legislative Council on 21 Mar 1952. Confirmed.

results.title: New Gold Coast Constitution Creates All-African Legislature
results.note: Constitution of 29 Apr 1954 established all-African 104-seat legislature; CPP won 72 seats.

results.title: National Liberation Movement Formed in Ashanti Opposing CPP
results.note: NLM formed 19 Sep 1954 in Kumasi by Ashanti leaders demanding federal constitution. Confirmed.

results.title: Ghana Declares Independence as Africa's First Sub-Saharan Free Nation
results.note: Independence declared 6 Mar 1957. Confirmed as first sub-Saharan African country to gain independence post-WWII.

results.title: Ghana Hosts All-African Peoples' Conference, Cementing Pan-African Role
results.note: AAPC held Dec 1958 in Accra; Lumumba attended and spoke. Confirmed.

results.title: Preventive Detention Act Curtails Political Opposition
results.note: PDA promulgated 18 Jul 1958; permitted up to 5-year detention without trial. Confirmed.

results.title: Ghana Becomes a Republic with Nkrumah as First President
results.note: Ghana became republic 1 Jul 1960; Nkrumah won presidential election over J.B. Danquah. Confirmed.

results.title: Volta River Project Construction Begins with US and World Bank Financing
results.note: Construction began 1961 after late-1961 financing agreement with Kaiser Aluminum, World Bank, US, UK. Confirmed.

results.title: Railway Workers Strike in Sekondi-Takoradi Suppressed
results.note: Strike began Sep 4 1961; railway and harbour workers in Sekondi-Takoradi; state of emergency declared; government suppressed. Confirmed.

results.title: Ghana Joins OAU as Founding Member at Addis Ababa Summit
results.note: OAU founded 25 May 1963 in Addis Ababa; Ghana founding member; Nkrumah's continental government demand rejected in favour of sovereignty-respecting charter. Confirmed.

results.title: Ghana Declared a One-Party State with Nkrumah as Life President
results.note: Referendum held 31 Jan 1964; reported 99.91% support; CPP sole party; Nkrumah president-for-life. Confirmed.

results.title: Akosombo Dam Completed, Creating Lake Volta
results.note: Dam was completed in 1965, not 1964. Construction ran 1961–1965; VALCO smelter commercial production started 1967. Year is wrong by one year.

results.title: Cocoa Price Collapse Deepens Ghana's Foreign Exchange Crisis
results.note: Cocoa price collapse in mid-1960s confirmed as major driver of Ghana's foreign exchange crisis under Nkrumah.

results.title: Military Coup Overthrows Nkrumah While He Is Abroad
results.note: Coup on 24 Feb 1966 led by Ankrah, Kotoka, Harlley. Nkrumah was en route to Hanoi via Beijing — the event says 'travelling to Hanoi', which is directionally accurate though he was actually in China when the coup occurred. Core facts (date, NLC, coup while abroad) confirmed.

results.title: Ghana Seeks IMF Emergency Assistance After Economic Collapse
results.note: First IMF agreement signed 17 May 1966; cedi devaluation and austerity imposed. Confirmed.

results.title: Second Republic Established — Busia Elected Prime Minister
results.note: Progress Party won Aug 1969 election; military handed power to Busia on 1 Oct 1969. Confirmed.

results.title: Cedi Devalued 44 Percent Under IMF Conditionality
results.note: Dec 1971 devaluation — 44% in dollar terms confirmed; triggered public anger and the Jan 1972 coup.

results.title: Colonel Acheampong Overthrows Busia in Bloodless Coup
results.note: Bloodless coup 13 Jan 1972; NRC established; Acheampong cited devaluation and mismanagement. Confirmed.

results.title: Ghana Repudiates Foreign Debts Under Economic Nationalism
results.note: NRC repudiated medium-term debts and reversed cedi devaluation in Feb 1972 under 'Operation Feed Yourself' nationalism. Confirmed.

results.title: Ghana's Economy Collapses with Triple-Digit Inflation and Shortages
results.note: Triple-digit inflation, cocoa production decline, and shortages in mid-1970s under Acheampong's NRC/SMC are well-documented.

results.title: General Akuffo Ousts Acheampong and Promises Elections
results.note: Palace coup 15 Jul 1978; Lt-Gen Akuffo assumed power, released political prisoners, promised elections. Confirmed.

results.title: Rawlings Leads AFRC Coup, Executes Former Heads of State
results.note: Coup 4 Jun 1979; AFRC executed Acheampong, Akuffo, Afrifa, and five others. Event says 'five other senior officers' — total was 8 executed including 3 former heads of state. Minor count detail; core claim confirmed.

results.title: Third Republic Established — Hilla Limann Elected President
results.note: Limann inaugurated 24 Sep 1979 (not Sep 24 as stated in event — date is correct). PNP ticket confirmed.

results.title: Rawlings Returns to Power in Second Coup, Establishes PNDC
results.note: Second coup 31 Dec 1981; PNDC established; Limann overthrown. Governed until 1993 — 11 years confirmed.

results.title: Economic Recovery Program Marks Shift to IMF-Backed Structural Adjustment
results.note: ERP launched Apr 1983 with IMF/World Bank support; ideological shift from revolutionary socialism confirmed.

results.title: Severe Drought and Nigeria's Expulsion of One Million Ghanaians
results.note: Drought and bushfires + Nigeria's Jan 1983 expulsion order confirmed; ~900,000–1.2 million Ghanaians returned. Event says 'approximately one million' — accurate.

results.title: Investment Code Reforms Attract Foreign Mining Capital
results.note: 1985–1986 investment code liberalisation attracted Ashanti Goldfields expansion and new foreign mining capital. Confirmed.

results.title: Ghana's ERP Recovery Earns World Bank 'Model Student' Designation
results.note: 1984–86 GDP growth averaged 6.3%; inflation fell from triple digits; World Bank held Ghana as model SAP success. Confirmed.

results.title: District Assembly Reform Expands Decentralised Governance
results.note: District assemblies created 1987 by PNDC; first nonpartisan district elections 1988. Confirmed.

results.title: National Commission for Democracy Consultations Open Path to Multiparty Rule
results.note: NCD consultations 1990 revealed popular demand for multiparty democracy; led directly to 1992 transition. Confirmed.

results.title: Fourth Republic Constitution Approved by Referendum
results.note: Referendum 28 Apr 1992; 93% approval; presidential system, two-term limit, multiparty democracy. Confirmed.

results.title: Rawlings Wins Presidential Election Transitioning to Civilian Leader
results.note: Rawlings won 58.4%; Boahen (NPP) alleged rigging; opposition boycotted parliamentary elections. Confirmed.

results.title: Fourth Republic Inaugurated — Ghana Stock Exchange Opens
results.note: Fourth Republic inaugurated 7 Jan 1993; Ghana Stock Exchange opened 1990 (formally commenced trading 1994). The GSE opened in 1990, not 1993 — slight inaccuracy in timing but Fourth Republic inauguration date confirmed.

results.title: Konkomba-Nanumba Ethnic Violence Kills Thousands in Northern Ghana
results.note: 1994 Guinea Fowl War; at least 1,000–2,000 killed, 150,000 displaced; land/chieftaincy disputes. Confirmed.

results.title: VAT Protests Turn Violent — Government Withdraws Tax
results.note: May 1995 'Kume Preko' protest; VAT introduced Mar 1995; deaths confirmed (search found 16 casualties total); Rawlings withdrew the VAT bill. Event says 'four demonstrators killed' — search found 16 casualties; minor discrepancy in death count but core facts confirmed.

results.title: Ashanti Goldfields Lists on London Stock Exchange
results.note: AGC's landmark 1996 listing was on the New York Stock Exchange (first African company on NYSE), not the London Stock Exchange. AGC had historic London presence since 1895 but the 'first African mining company' milestone was the 1996 NYSE listing, not a new London listing.

results.title: Rawlings Re-elected in Credible, Internationally Observed Election
results.note: Rawlings won ~57% in credible 1996 election with full opposition participation and international observer approval. Confirmed.

results.title: Kufuor Wins Election in Ghana's First Peaceful Inter-Party Power Transfer
results.note: Kufuor defeated Mills in Dec 2000 runoff; first inter-party transfer of power since independence. Confirmed.

results.title: Ghana Qualifies for HIPC Debt Relief, Freeing Resources for Social Spending
results.note: Kufuor government applied for HIPC Mar 2001; completion point reached Jul 2004; ~$3.7B debt relief. Event says '2001' for initial qualification — accurate. Confirmed.

results.title: National Health Insurance Act Creates Public Health Coverage Scheme
results.note: NHIS established under National Health Insurance Act 650 of 2003, not 2002 as stated. The year is off by one. Core content (payroll + VAT financing, social policy milestone) is accurate but the year is wrong. Marking UNVERIFIED due to date discrepancy.

results.title: Kufuor Re-elected — Democratic Consolidation Confirmed
results.note: Kufuor won second term in 2004 over Mills; declared free and fair. Confirmed.

results.title: Millennium Challenge Compact Brings $547 Million in US Development Funding
results.note: MCC compact confirmed; $547M five-year agreement for agricultural and transport infrastructure. Confirmed.

results.title: Commercial Oil Discovered in Jubilee Field Offshore Ghana
results.note: Jubilee field discovered Jun 2007 by Kosmos Energy; field ~60km offshore; Tullow Oil co-developer. Reserve estimates of 600M–1.8B barrels cited in event match early public estimates. Confirmed.

results.title: Mills Wins Closest Election in Ghanaian History by Under 0.5 Percent
results.note: Mills won runoff 28 Dec 2008 by ~40,000 votes (50.23% vs 49.77%); closest election in Ghana's history. Event says 'fewer than 50,000 votes' — confirmed.

results.title: Obama Visits Ghana, Highlighting Democratic Model in Africa
results.note: Obama visited Accra 11 Jul 2009; first sub-Saharan Africa trip; parliament speech confirmed; 'Africa needs strong institutions' theme confirmed.

results.title: Ghana Enacts Petroleum Revenue Management Act Ahead of Oil Production
results.note: The PRMA was passed in 2011, not 2009. Parliament passed Act 815 in 2011 ahead of revenue flows. The event describes real policy content but the year is wrong.

results.title: Ghana Begins Commercial Oil Production from Jubilee Field
results.note: First oil 15 Dec 2010; FPSO Kwame Nkrumah confirmed; initial capacity ~55,000 bpd ramping to 120,000. Event says 70,000 bpd — within ramp-up range. Confirmed.

results.title: President Atta Mills Dies in Office — Mahama Assumes Presidency
results.note: Mills died 24 Jul 2012; Mahama sworn in same day; first Ghanaian president to die in office. Confirmed.

results.title: Supreme Court Upholds Mahama's Election After Landmark Judicial Review
results.note: NPP petition filed; SC ruled 29 Aug 2013 (5–4) upholding Mahama; process took ~8 months. Confirmed.

results.title: Ghana Returns to IMF for $918 Million Bailout as Fiscal Crisis Deepens
results.note: IMF approved $918M ECF arrangement Apr 2015 (for 2014-initiated programme); cedi depreciation and fiscal imbalances confirmed.

results.title: Dumsor Power Crisis Severely Disrupts Ghana's Economy
results.note: Dumsor crisis peak 2015; up to 24-hour daily outages; Akosombo low water levels and utility distress confirmed as causes. Confirmed.

results.title: Akufo-Addo Wins Election Ending Mahama Tenure in Peaceful Transfer
results.note: Akufo-Addo won Dec 2016; Mahama conceded; dumsor and economic dissatisfaction cited. Confirmed.

results.title: Free Senior High School Policy Launched — Major Education Overhaul
results.note: Free SHS launched Sep 2017; enrollment surged ~17-31%; double-track system introduced. Confirmed.

results.title: Bank of Ghana Launches Major Banking Sector Cleanup
results.note: Banking cleanup 2017–2019; licences revoked, capital requirements raised, cost >20 billion cedis. Confirmed.

results.title: Ghana Among First Signatories of African Continental Free Trade Area
results.note: Ghana signed AfCFTA in Kigali Mar 2018 and was among first to ratify; AfCFTA secretariat headquartered in Accra. Confirmed.

results.title: Akufo-Addo Re-elected During COVID-19 Pandemic in Credible Poll
results.note: Akufo-Addo won Dec 2020 election; COVID protocols; international observers declared free and fair. Confirmed.

results.title: Ghana First Country Globally to Receive COVAX Vaccines
results.note: Ghana received first COVAX shipment 24 Feb 2021; 600,000 AstraZeneca doses. Confirmed by WHO, UNICEF, CNN.

results.title: Ghana Faces Worst Economic Crisis Since the 1980s — Cedi Loses Over 50 Percent
results.note: 2022 crisis: cedi lost >50%, inflation surged above 50%, debt unsustainable; IMF programme sought. Confirmed.

results.title: Domestic Debt Exchange Restructures Government Bonds, Shocks Financial Sector
results.note: DDEP launched 5 Dec 2022; extended maturities and reduced coupon rates; banks, pension funds, insurers affected. Confirmed.

results.title: Ghana Agrees $3 Billion IMF Extended Credit Facility
results.note: $3B ECF approved May 2023; preliminary bilateral creditor agreements including China and Paris Club confirmed. Confirmed.

results.title: John Mahama Wins Presidential Election — NDC Returns to Power
results.note: Mahama won Dec 2024 with 56.55%; NDC won parliamentary majority; Bawumia conceded morning after; peaceful transfer. Confirmed.

results.title: Ghana Finalises External Debt Restructuring with Eurobond Holders
results.note: Search found Ghana completed $1.4B in scheduled Eurobond payments in 2025 and OCC MOU effective Oct 2025, but the comprehensive 'finalisation' of all ~$13B Eurobond restructuring described in the event is not fully confirmed. Restructuring agreement reached in 2024 but characterisation of full finalisation in 2025 is premature per available data.

results.title: Galamsey Illegal Mining Crisis Threatens Water and Cocoa Farmland
results.note: Galamsey crisis ongoing into 2025; Pra, Offin, Ankobra rivers contaminated; mercury confirmed; cocoa production impacted. Confirmed.
